quantum_risk.estimate_basis: No qubit estimate is computed for this primitive.

classical_risk.basis: Size unknown, so classical strength cannot be assessed.

padding_risk.weakness: Deterministic encryption: the same plaintext always gives the same ciphertext, so there is no semantic security. This is a classical weakness, independent of Shor's algorithm.
padding_risk.source: Vaibhav: textbook RSA with no padding, confirmed in the code

recommended_pqc.rationale: ML-KEM is a key-encapsulation mechanism: use it to establish a shared secret, then encrypt the data with AES-256-GCM (do not use bare RSA-style encryption). Parameter set 768 targets NIST security category 3. If this RSA is used for signatures instead, use ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204).

notes: Key size is not verified; the qubit estimate and classical assessment depend on it.

quantum_risk.estimate_basis: Logical qubits to factor a 256-bit modulus with the 2n+3 circuit (Beauregard 2003). Logical qubits only: error-correction overhead is excluded, so physical qubit counts are far higher.

classical_risk.basis: A 256-bit modulus can be attacked with ordinary hardware or rented cloud time. No quantum computer is needed.

quantum_risk.estimate_basis: No qubit estimate is computed for this primitive.

classical_risk.basis: A 256-bit hash output is adequate classically.

padding_risk.source: Padding schemes apply to RSA encryption and signatures.

recommended_pqc.rationale: Grover's algorithm halves preimage resistance; a 256-bit or larger output keeps about 128-bit security.

references: Shor, P. W. (1997). Polynomial-time algorithms for prime factorization and discrete logarithms on a quantum computer. SIAM J. Comput. 26(5), 1484-1509.
Grover, L. K. (1996). A fast quantum mechanical algorithm for database search. Proc. 28th ACM STOC, 212-219.
Beauregard, S. (2003). Circuit for Shor's algorithm using 2n+3 qubits. Quantum Information & Computation 3(2), 175-185. arXiv:quant-ph/0205095.
Gidney, C. and Ekera, M. (2021). How to factor 2048 bit RSA integers in 8 hours using 20 million noisy qubits. Quantum 5, 433. arXiv:1905.09749.
NIST FIPS 203 (2024). Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard (ML-KEM).
NIST FIPS 204 (2024). Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard (ML-DSA).
notes: Quantum risk, classical risk and padding risk are reported separately. Padding weaknesses such as textbook RSA are classical problems, not consequences of Shor's algorithm.
Logical-qubit estimates use the 2n+3 circuit for factoring an n-bit modulus. They exclude error-correction overhead, so physical qubit counts are much larger.
All quantum demonstrations in this project run on a simulator at toy sizes. Resource figures for RSA-1024/2048 are published estimates, not measurements.
Grover's algorithm is a quadratic speed-up, not a full break: symmetric and hash primitives keep about half their classical security bits.
